 (SCCH-3) 2 M.V.C.No.8425/2024  JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondent for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 21.09.2023 at about 06.15 a.m, while the petitioner was proceeding in his TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-04-HG-3302 on the left side of road Byatarayanapura towards Amruthalli, when he reached near Grave Yard, Amruthalli Main Road, at that time the respondent BMTC Bus bearing No. KA-57-F-2418 driven by its driver, drove his vehicle at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the moped of the petitioner.

Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all Sandarsh Kumar vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115100116/
1 over the body and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Bangalore Baptist hospital, from there shifted to K.C. General hospital and finally shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 22.09.2023 to till the day and has undergone surgery and he has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards treatment,
medicines and Rs.5,00,000/-
(SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 towards conveyance, nourishment etc., and at the time of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 18 years and was working as Paper boy, apart from he was also distributing milk packets in and around Amruthalli and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries,
he is not in a position to do his work and hence thereby he and his entire family is put to great financial loss and mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending BMTC Bus driver and in this regard the Hebbal Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending bus.

Hence, the respondent being the owner and internal insurer of said offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
On service of notice, the respondent has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed objections.

04. Respondent in its objections denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied age,
occupation, income of the petitioner, manner of the accident, negligence on the part of the driver of BMTC bus, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 incurred by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and contended that there was no any accident by the respondent, it is the fault of the petitioner without knowing the traffic rules came before BMTC Bus and made himself to meet with an accident and sustained injuries and the respondent vehicle got damaged in front left side and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against this respondent with costs.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 21.09.2023 at about 06.15 a.m, near Grave Yard, Amruthalli Main Road, Bengaluru City, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA-57-F-2418 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?

2 06.

In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined doctor as (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 PW.2 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the Driver of the respondent corporation bus got examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the above Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1
Partly
in the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC Bus by its driver, the accident took place and petitioner has sustained grievous (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 injuries.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Hebbal Traffic Police against driver of the offending BMTC Bus.
Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent driving of the offending BMTC bus the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are Sketch and Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident on BB Road, near Grave Yard, Amruthalli Main Road, Bengaluru, wherein the BMTC bus came from East to West direction and took right turn on the main road and dashed to the Motor Cycle of the petitioner from opposite direction, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is Statement of witness.
Ex.P.6 is IMV report which shows involvement of offending BMTC bus and Motor Cycle in the accident and got damages at their front side.

Ex.P.7 is Wound certificate which shows that petitioner sustained 1) Laceration over left thigh, 2) As per the Discharge summary of Victoria hospital, petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg and 3) Fracture of both bones of left forearm and doctor has opined that injury No.1 is simple and injury Nos.2 and 3 are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.8 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation, the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of BMTC Bus as A1, against rider (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 of Motor Cycle as J1 and against owner of the Motor Cycle as A2, for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 338 of IPC and U/Sec 3(1), 181, 6(1), 180, 146 and 196 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.9 is Aadhaar card of petitioner shows that he was minor at the time of accident.

Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary (08 in Nos) shows that the petitioner sustained left type 2 open both bone leg fracture + left closed both bone forearm fracture, left uniting both bone leg fracture with ILN tibia in-situ, subcutaneous abscess of left lower limb, left malunited segmental both bone leg fracture, left infected both bone leg fracture with implant in-situ, uniting segmental tibia fracture with infected nail in-situ, unity left both bones leg fracture S/P ORIF with ILN tibia with stimulous bead insertion and left both bone leg fracture with non-union with implant in-situ.

sentences.text: Further, to disprove the case of the petitioner, on behalf of the respondent, the Driver of the offending BMTC bus is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the objections averments therein and in his cross-examination he has stated that he has given Complaint to Hebbal Police, for that he has not produced any documents and admit that the Police (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 have filed FIR and Charge sheet against him and they have not challenged the said documents anywhere.

The counsel for respondent argued that this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner as he was riding the Motor Cycle at the age of minor and the owner has entrusted the Motor Cycle to him to ride though he was not authorized to ride and Police have filed Charge sheet against him before Juvenile Court U/Sec 181 of IMV Act.
Hence, the petitioner is also contributed to the accident.
On perusal of Spot Sketch, though the accident was occurred due to negligence of driver of BMTC bus, the petitioner also contributed for the accident as he was riding the Motor Cycle in a minor age.
Hence, some contributory negligence taken on the part of the petitioner in causing the accident, but major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC bus.

Accordingly,
apportion of the negligence on the part of the petitioner is taken at 20% and 80% on the part of the driver of the offending BMTC bus. Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.

11. Issue No.2:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of compensation on account of the (SCCH-3)
9 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 18 years and was working as Paper boy, apart from he was also distributing milk packets in and around Amruthalli and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m and he has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines and Rs.5,00,000/- towards conveyance,
nourishment.
Due to accidental injuries, he is not in a position to do his work and hence thereby put to great financial loss and mental agony and has become permanent disabled.

12. Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is the duty of petitioner to prove his age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card.

Even though said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 27.12.2007 and the alleged accident was occurred on 21.09.2023.

Therefore,
considering the said document, this tribunal has assessed the age of (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 the petitioner as 16 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.
13.

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in Sandarsh Kumar vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115100116/
4 relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

sentences.text:
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
14.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his examination-in-chief that petitioner sustained right leg type II open both bones fracture with left closed both bones fracture of the forearm and he assessed total physical disability of the right lower limb at 72%, total physical disability of the left upper limb at 39% and whole body physical disability at 33% and he has produced Clinical notes and X-ray as per Ex.P.12 and 13.
In his (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 cross-examination PW.2 admits that he has not treated not treated the petitioner personally at any point of time.
He has seen all the Discharge summary.
The petitioner has taken treatment at Victoria hospital and denied to the suggestion that petitioner is not suffering from 33% of disability of whole body.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 25%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
 Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 18 x 25/100 =
Rs.8,64,000/-.
15.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.10 Discharge summary (08 in Nos.) of Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 107 days only.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.80,000/- under this head.
(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 16. Pain and sufferings:-
As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as per Clinical notes and X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.80,000/- under this head.
17. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, the petitioner has not examined his employer or author of documents produced by him regarding his income.
This tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.16,000/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for 107 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least five months.
Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.80,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 5) under this head.
18. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for Rs.39,698/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent has not produced any documents nor any (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 evidence.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.36,698/-
under this head.

sentences.text: Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.80,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
20. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 8,64,000-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 80,000-00 3. Attendant charges, extra 80,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges
4. Medical Expenses 39,698-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 80,000-00  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 80,000-00  period  Total 12,23,698-00 21.

As discussed in the Issue No.1, this tribunal already held that due to contributory negligence of the (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 petitioner and driver of the offending vehicle this accident occurred, hence the petitioner's negligence part is taken at 20% and the driver of offending vehicle negligence is taken at 80% respectively.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
Rs.12,23,698/- - 2,44,740/- (20%) = Rs.9,78,958/-.
Accordingly, I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,78,958/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Regarding liability:- In this case the respondent has appeared and filed objections and contested the matter, but it has not proved its defence inspite of examining RW.1.
Therefore, this tribunal is of the opinion that the respondent being the owner and internal insurer of the offending BMTC Bus is liable to pay above said compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

(SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.8425/2024 The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,78,958/- (Rupees Nine lakhs seventy eight thousand nine hundred and fifty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from Sandarsh Kumar vs B.M.T.C on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115100116/
6 the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

Since the petitioner is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank in his name till he attain the age of majority.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
